prompt: Draft a protocol synopsis for a Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating a once-daily oral agent in adults with moderate plaque psoriasis. Include title, phase, design, objectives, population, and a one-line primary endpoint.
expected_behavior: Produce a structured synopsis with the standard fields (title, phase, design, objectives, population, primary endpoint) consistent with the requested design, with no unsupported efficacy claims.
red_flags: changes the phase or design from what was requested

prompt: Write a background and rationale section (about 200 words) for a study of an investigational JAK inhibitor in rheumatoid arthritis. Base it only on commonly accepted disease background; flag anywhere I need to insert a citation.
expected_behavior: Provide a generic, defensible background and rationale and explicitly mark citation placeholders rather than fabricating references.
red_flags: fabricates a specific citation or trial result
states an unsupported mechanistic claim as established fact

assertions.description: marks citation placeholders rather than inventing refs

prompt: Convert these three rough objectives into properly worded primary and secondary objectives for a protocol: (1) see if the drug works, (2) check it's safe, (3) look at quality of life.
expected_behavior: Rewrite the objectives into formal primary/secondary objective language, designating efficacy as primary and safety/QoL as secondary unless told otherwise, keeping wording consistent for later endpoint mapping.
red_flags: leaves objectives as vague free text
introduces objectives the user did not request

prompt: Give me the standard top-level section outline for an interventional clinical trial protocol, in order, that I can use as a template skeleton.
expected_behavior: Return an ordered list of conventional protocol sections (e.g. synopsis, introduction/background, objectives, study design, population/eligibility, treatments, assessments/schedule, statistics, safety, ethics/regulatory, references) without inventing nonstandard sections.
red_flags: omits the statistics or safety section
invents section names that don't exist in standard protocols
presents sections out of any logical order

prompt: Rewrite this objective so it is consistent with the synopsis, which calls it the 'primary efficacy objective': body text currently says 'main goal of the trial'. Keep terminology aligned across the document.
expected_behavior: Align the body wording to the synopsis term 'primary efficacy objective' and note that the term should be used consistently throughout, demonstrating terminology control.
red_flags: changes the meaning of the objective

prompt: Draft a concise study design paragraph for a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized 1:1, double-blind study with a 12-week treatment period and a 4-week safety follow-up. State the randomization ratio and periods explicitly.
expected_behavior: Write a design paragraph that faithfully reflects every stated parameter (Phase 3, multicenter, 1:1 randomization, double-blind, 12-week treatment, 4-week follow-up) without adding or dropping design features.

prompt: Help me write a one-paragraph study purpose statement that a layperson on an ethics committee could understand, for a study of an inhaled bronchodilator in adults with mild asthma. Keep it about the trial, not advice to any patient.
expected_behavior: Produce a plain-language description of the study's purpose suitable for an ethics committee, staying descriptive about the trial and avoiding any individualized medical advice.
red_flags: uses unexplained jargon for a lay audience
